prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP’s 2015 manifesto centres on leaving the EU to “take back control” of laws, borders and spending, and redirect money to domestic priorities without raising taxes or debt. Savings would come from ending the UK’s net EU contribution, cutting foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrapping HS2, replacing the Barnett formula, tackling “health tourism,” and reducing government and quango costs. Independently costed plans (Cebr) underpin pledges to invest in the NHS, social care, policing/borders and tax cuts.

Economy and tax
- Raise personal allowance to at least £13,000; remove income tax on minimum wage.
- Scrap inheritance tax; lift 40% threshold to £55,000; add a 30% band between £43,500–£55,000; aim for flatter 20/30/40 rates.
- Toughen action on multinationals’ tax avoidance; restore UK tax sovereignty.
- Replace Barnett formula with needs-based funding; cut overseas aid to 0.2% GNI.
- Scrap HS2; cut Westminster costs; abolish some departments/quangos.

Immigration and borders
- Leave the EU to end free movement. Introduce an Australian-style points system; five‑year moratorium on unskilled immigration; limit highly skilled work visas to ~50,000/year.
- +2,500 Border Agency staff; full entry/exit checks; no amnesty for illegal migrants.
- Five-year qualification for migrants’ access to benefits and non‑urgent NHS care.
- Revoke citizenship gained by fraud; act against citizens fighting with terror groups.

NHS and social care
- Extra £12bn for the NHS over five years; 8,000 more GPs, 20,000 nurses, 3,000 midwives; GP pilots in A&E; £1.5bn for mental health and dementia; free hospital parking.
- Clamp down on “health tourism”; exclude NHS from TTIP; scrap PFI use; reform regulators and introduce a “Licence to Manage.”
- Increase social care funding by £1.2bn/year; integrate health and social care under the NHS; dignity code; end 15‑minute visits; better pay/conditions for home‑care staff.

Welfare, pensions and carers
- Scrap the bedroom tax; keep Housing Benefit for under‑25s; strengthen fraud enforcement; 800 advisers at foodbanks.
- Move disability assessments to GPs/specialists.
- Flexible state pension window; boost pensions advice; criminalise pension cold‑calling.
- Raise Carer’s Allowance to match JSA (+£572/year).

Education and childcare
- More school diversity (grammar, technical, vocational); abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; reduce teacher workload; first aid in PSHE.
- STEMM degrees fee‑free for UK students who work and pay tax in the UK for 5 years.
- Deregulate childcare to reduce costs; require wrap‑around care 8am–6pm in primaries.
- Shared parenting presumption; grandparent access; overhaul child protection.

Housing and planning
- Prioritise brownfield: national register, remediation grants, stamp duty relief; bring empty homes back into use; protect green belt; local referenda on major schemes.
- Restrict social housing and Help to Buy/Right to Buy to citizens (with Armed Forces exception for non‑citizens).

Energy and environment
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; end subsidies for new wind/solar; support coal, nuclear, hydro and shale with safeguards; abolish green levies to cut bills.

Transport
- Scrap HS2; consider Manston Airport; restrict speed cameras to safety sites; oppose road pricing and EU eCall; scrap DCPC; double HGV levy for foreign trucks; VED exemption for 25+ year classics.

Crime, justice and defence
- +6,000 frontline posts across police, prisons and borders; leave the ECHR; UK Bill of Rights; scrap European Arrest Warrant; tougher sentencing review; decriminalise TV licence non‑payment; deport foreign criminals.
- Raise defence spending to at least 2% of GDP, retain Trident, rebuild capabilities, create a Director of National Intelligence, exempt troops on operations from income tax; oppose an EU army.

Trade, politics and culture
- Brexit via referendum and Article 50; seek UK–EU free trade deal; regain WTO seat; pursue global FTAs.
- Political reform: citizens’ initiative referendums, real right of recall, open primaries, select committee vetoes on appointments/spending, proportional voting, end postal voting on demand.
- Promote integration and English language; protect free speech; bank holidays for St George’s and St David’s Days.
